newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks mixed in becalmed London trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks mixed in becalmed London trading.

text.p: U.S. stocks were quiet in London trading on Monday, with activity severely restricted by public holidays in most European centres indluding Frankfurt, Paris and Zurich, dealers said.

After Friday's tumble on Wall Street, which left the Dow down 1.9 percent, dealers said U.S. markets were likely to continue cautious ahead of Tuesday's expected quarter-point rise in short-term interest rates by the Federal Reserve's decision-making committee.
Friday's decline came after the Dow closed at a record 7,333.55 on May 15 and highlighted the market's continuing volatility, sparked by speculation over rising interest rates.
Yet dealers said markets could react positively to the expected quarter-point rate rise, if it was seen as reducing the chances of further increases later this year.
"Probably a quarter point is factored in and the market could be more upset if it doesn't happen," said one dealer in U.S. stocks here.
"With the uncertainty out of the way we will be able to crack on."

The June futures contract on the S&P 500 index was trading at 835.35 by 1030 GMT, up from 829.75 at Friday's close, while the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was unchanged at 96-15/32, yielding 6.90 percent.
No key U.S. economic reports were due to be released on Monday.

Among individual stocks, dealers said the early attention would likely be focused on Oracle and Netscape after reports late last week that Oracle had agreed to buy a unit of the Internet access company.

Industry executives told Reuters late on Friday Oracle planned to buy Netscape's Navio Communications Inc unit, that designs software for browsing the world wide web through devices such as television sets and video games machines.
Netscape shares plummeted $5-5/16 to $29-1/4 on Friday after the company warned of slower revenue and earnings growth.

Elsewhere dealers said major U.S. stocks were stuck around Friday's close, with little trading interest either way. "There is not a lot of professional interest around," said one, "prices are mixed around the close and we are expecting a quiet day ahead of the Fed meeting."
